next.name: Threat Group-3390
next.headline: Threat Group-3390: a long-running espionage group known by many names, from watering holes to HyperBro
next.in_short: Threat Group-3390, also called Emissary Panda and APT27, is described by researchers and Germany's BfV as a Chinese espionage group. Reports span 2015 to 2025 and cover watering holes, HyperBro and server exploits.

sentences.t: Threat Group-3390 is also tracked as Emissary Panda, APT27, LuckyMouse, Iron Tiger, BRONZE UNION, Earth Smilodon and Linen Typhoon.
Dell SecureWorks researchers designated the group Threat Group 3390 and nicknamed it Emissary Panda. The report describes it as believed to be based in China.
Germany's Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV) describes APT27, also known as Emissary Panda, as a Chinese cyberespionage group.
Symantec's Threat Hunter Team calls the group Budworm, also known as LuckyMouse, Emissary Panda and APT27. It says the group is believed to have been active since at least 2013.
In 2015, SecureWorks said most targets were in the automotive, electronic, aerospace, energy and pharmaceutical industries. At least 50 organizations in the US and the United Kingdom had data stolen.
The same report lists defense contractors, colleges and universities, law firms and political organizations among the targets.
Symantec says Budworm often focuses on government, technology and defense organizations. In August 2023 it attacked a Middle Eastern telecommunications organization and an Asian government.
The BfV says APT27 has repeatedly attacked German companies since at least March 2021.

In 2015 the group mainly used watering hole attacks launched from over 100 compromised legitimate websites. SecureWorks said it relied on old vulnerabilities, including CVE-2011-3544 and CVE-2010-0738, and used the PlugX remote access tool.
The BfV says the 2021 attacks exploited unpatched, internet-exposed servers running Microsoft Exchange and Zoho ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus. The final payload was HyperBro.
A malware entry says HyperBro is a remote access trojan that typically has three or more components, including a genuine loader and an encrypted, compressed payload.
Symantec says Budworm ran its SysUpdate backdoor by DLL sideloading. It also used living-off-the-land and publicly available tools to map networks and dump credentials.
The catalogue record also lists tools including PlugX, China Chopper, Cobalt Strike, Mimikatz, Impacket and ZxShell.
SecureWorks unveiled its report on the group at the Black Hat conference in August 2015.
Symantec says the August 2023 attacks used an updated SysUpdate backdoor. It says only credential harvesting was seen on infected machines, so the activity may have been stopped early.

In July 2025 Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported exploitation of on-premises SharePoint servers. It named Linen Typhoon, one of this group's aliases in the catalogue, among Chinese nation-state actors using the flaws.
eSentire noted that a ransomware intrusion resembled Emissary Panda techniques. It said it has no strong evidence linking the two and that the overlap could be a false flag.
Patch internet-facing servers promptly and watch for unusual sideloaded libraries and credential theft tools.
